docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Infrastructure Engineering

Knowledge Base

Production-grade notes, documentation, and references across VMware virtualization, enterprise storage, cloud, storage area networking, and disaster recovery.

Christos Anastasiadis Infrastructure Engineer LinkedIn  ·  Email 1,100+ Knowledge articles 30+ Technology domains VMware · Dell · Pure · NetApp Core platforms AWS · Azure Cloud platforms

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text: Virtualization VMware VCF, vCenter, ESXi, vSAN, NSX, VxRail, and Aria. Storage Dell, Pure, NetApp — block, file, object, and replication. Cloud AWS and Azure — identity, compute, networking, storage, and cost. SAN Cisco, Brocade, zoning, fabrics, ISLs, ports, and host paths. Compute Windows Server, Linux, host operations, and server support. Networking Routing, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, and connectivity references.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Operations Playbooks Daily checks, triage, maintenance windows, and post-change validation. Automation PowerShell, Python, Ansible, Terraform, and GitHub Actions. Monitoring Dashboards, alerting, health monitoring, and metrics baselines. Security Identity, certificates, privileged access, compliance, and audit. Disaster Recovery DR tools, failover, failback, runbooks, and validation. Data Protection Backup, restore, retention, recovery, and validation references.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: Tools ServiceNow, Jira, Confluence, Git, and daily admin tooling. Standards Naming, build, configuration, security, and zoning standards. Protocols Fibre Channel, iSCSI, NFS, SMB, DNS, DHCP, NTP, SNMP, LDAP, TLS. Certifications Certification paths, study notes, and practice references. Architecture HA, DR, network, storage, and cloud design references. Lifecycle Onboarding, decommissioning, migrations, and upgrade readiness.

docs.title: Quality rules
docs.text:
• Every page should be reachable from nav or a card.

  • Recovery priority
  • Data consistency requirements

  • Failover tested
  • Backup verified

docs.title: Overview

• Redundancy
  • Failover

  • Health monitoring
  • Automatic recovery

docs.title: Validation Checks

  • Monitoring alerts configured

  5. Document recovery behavior

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This process ensures changes are reviewed and approved before implementation.

docs.text:
• Standard change
  • Normal change
  • Emergency change

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Review change details
  2. Assess risk and impact
  3. Obtain stakeholder approval
  4. Record approval decision

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Change communication ensures stakeholders are informed before, during, and after changes.

docs.title: Communication Steps
docs.text:
• Notify affected teams
  • Provide maintenance schedule
  • Send completion update

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Prepare communication message
  2. Send notification
  3. Confirm receipt
  4. Provide status updates

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A change request documents planned modifications to infrastructure, applications, or configurations.

docs.title: Required Information
docs.text:
• Change description
  • Systems affected
  • Risk assessment
  • Maintenance window
  • Rollback plan

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Submit change request
  2. Review risk and impact
  3. Obtain approval
  4. Schedule implementation
  5. Document results

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Change validation confirms systems function correctly after a change.

docs.title: Validation Checks
docs.text:
• Services operational
  • Monitoring alerts cleared
  • Performance metrics normal

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Perform system checks
  2. Confirm user access
  3. Review logs
  4. Close change ticket

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure defines steps to deploy infrastructure or application changes safely.

docs.title: Pre-Deployment Checks
docs.text:
• Verify backups completed
  • Confirm maintenance window
  • Validate system health

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Start deployment
  2. Monitor progress
  3. Validate services
  4. Document results

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Emergency changes address critical incidents requiring immediate action.

docs.title: Trigger Conditions
docs.text:
• Service outage
  • Security incident
  • System failure

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify issue
  2. Notify stakeholders
  3. Implement fix
  4. Document change
  5. Perform post-incident review

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Release management coordinates deployment of new software, updates, and infrastructure changes.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review scheduled releases
  • Confirm deployment readiness
  • Validate rollback procedures

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Plan release scope
  2. Validate testing completed
  3. Schedule deployment
  4. Monitor release execution
  5. Confirm service stability

docs.text: AWS EC2 provides virtual machine compute capacity in AWS. It supports application hosting, batch processing, automation workers, jump hosts, and infrastructure services.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review instance status checks
  • Check CPU, memory, and disk trends
  • Validate backups and AMIs
  • Review security groups
  • Confirm patch compliance

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
aws ec2 describe-instances
aws ec2 describe-instance-status
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name CPUUtilization
aws ssm describe-instance-information

docs.title: Upgrade Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create AMI or snapshot
  2. Confirm application owner approval
  3. Patch through SSM or maintenance process
  4. Reboot if required
  5. Validate instance and application health

docs.title: AWS Networking
docs.text: VPC VPC layout, routing, address planning, endpoints, and controls. Subnets Subnet design, route scope, availability zones, and segmentation. Route Tables Routing paths, default routes, private routes, and validation. Internet Gateway Public internet routing and edge connectivity. NAT Gateway Private subnet outbound internet access and troubleshooting. VPC Endpoints Private service access, gateway endpoints, and interface endpoints. Security Groups Instance-level firewall rules and access validation. Network ACLs Subnet-level stateless filtering and traffic control. Elastic Load Balancer ALB, NLB, target groups, listeners, and health checks. Route 53 Hosted zones, DNS records, routing policies, and resolver notes. VPC Flow Logs Network traffic logging, query patterns, and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: AWS S3 is object storage used for backups, logs, application data, static sites, data lakes, and archive workflows.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review bucket access policies
  • Check lifecycle rules
  • Confirm replication status
  • Review storage growth
  • Validate encryption settings

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
aws s3 ls
aws s3api list-buckets
aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket BUCKET_NAME
aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket BUCKET_NAME

docs.title: Upgrade Workflow
docs.text:
S3 is a managed service. Operational changes usually involve lifecycle, replication, encryption, policy, and logging updates.

  1. Export current bucket policy
  2. Review access and encryption impact
  3. Apply change
  4. Validate application access
  5. Confirm logging and replication remain healthy

docs.text: Azure Virtual Machines provide compute resources for Windows and Linux workloads in Microsoft Azure.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review VM health
  • Check disk capacity and performance
  • Validate backup status
  • Review update compliance
  • Confirm monitoring alerts

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
az vm list -o table
az vm get-instance-view --resource-group RG --name VM
az monitor metrics list --resource VM_RESOURCE_ID --metric Percentage CPU
az backup job list --resource-group RG --vault-name VAULT

docs.title: Upgrade Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm backup restore point
  2. Validate maintenance window
  3. Apply OS patches
  4. Reboot if required
  5. Confirm VM and application health

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Backup validation ensures recovery capability and data integrity.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify successful backup jobs
  • Confirm restore points exist
  • Check repository capacity

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
Get-VBRJob
bpdbjobs
qlist job

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify backup set
  2. Perform test restore
  3. Validate recovered data
  4. Document results

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Data classification categorizes information based on sensitivity and protection requirements.

docs.title: Classification Levels
docs.text:
• Public
  • Internal
  • Confidential
  • Restricted

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify classification labels applied
  • Confirm access restrictions
  • Review audit logs

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify data type
  2. Assign classification level
  3. Apply protection controls
  4. Monitor data usage

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Encryption protects data at rest and in transit.

docs.title: Encryption Areas
docs.text:
• Disk encryption
  • Database encryption
  • Network encryption
  • Backup encryption

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify encryption enabled
  • Confirm key management functioning
  • Check certificate validity

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Enable encryption
  2. Store keys securely
  3. Monitor encryption status
  4. Rotate keys periodically

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Data governance defines how data is managed, protected, and controlled across systems.

docs.title: Governance Controls
docs.text:
• Data ownership defined
  • Access policies enforced
  • Retention rules applied
  • Audit logging enabled

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review data access logs
  • Confirm policy compliance
  • Validate audit records

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Define governance policies
  2. Assign data ownership
  3. Monitor compliance
  4. Review audit results

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This policy defines how long data is stored to meet business, legal, and compliance requirements.

docs.title: Standard Retention Periods
docs.text:
• Production data: Based on business requirements
  • Backup data: 30–365 days
  • Logs: 90–365 days
  • Audit records: 1–7 years

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify retention policies applied
  • Confirm archive jobs completed
  • Check storage utilization

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify data classification
  2. Apply retention policy
  3. Monitor storage usage
  4. Review compliance requirements

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Key management controls encryption keys used to protect sensitive data.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify key rotation schedule
  • Confirm backup of key store
  • Review access logs

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Generate encryption keys
  2. Store keys securely
  3. Rotate keys periodically
  4. Revoke compromised keys

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Recovery testing confirms systems can be restored after failure.

docs.title: Test Types
docs.text:
• File restore
  • VM recovery
  • Database restore
  • Full system recovery

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify scheduled tests completed
  • Confirm recovery procedures documented

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Select recovery scenario
  2. Perform recovery test
  3. Validate system functionality
  4. Document recovery results

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook confirms database backups are successful and recoverable.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm backup job schedule
  • Identify backup location
  • Verify storage capacity

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
ls -lh /backup/database
grep backup /var/log/messages
df -h

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm backup file exists
  2. Perform test restore if required
  3. Verify database integrity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook monitors database storage growth and prevents capacity exhaustion.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm database size
  • Identify storage thresholds
  • Review growth trends

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
du -sh /var/lib/mysql
df -h

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm storage capacity sufficient
  2. Identify growth patterns
  3. Plan storage expansion if required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure defines steps to promote a standby database during failure.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm primary database failure
  • Verify standby readiness
  • Notify application teams

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
systemctl stop primary-db
systemctl start standby-db

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm standby promoted
  2. Confirm application connectivity restored
  3. Monitor system performance

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook verifies database availability, performance, and connectivity.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm database instance name
  • Identify application dependencies
  • Check recent alerts

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
systemctl status mysqld
ps aux | grep postgres
netstat -tulnp | grep 5432

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm database service running
  2. Confirm client connectivity
  3. Review database logs

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure covers routine database maintenance tasks.

docs.title: Maintenance Tasks
docs.text:
• Index optimization
  • Log cleanup
  • Statistics update
  • Backup verification

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
vacuum analyze
mysqlcheck --optimize database

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm maintenance completed
  2. Confirm database performance stable
  3. Document maintenance results

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook identifies performance bottlenecks affecting database workloads.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm affected queries
  • Check system resource usage
  • Review recent configuration changes

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
top
iostat -x 1
vmstat 1

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm resource utilization stabilized
  2. Confirm query response time improved
  3. Document root cause

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook verifies replication status between primary and secondary database nodes.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Identify replication topology
  • Confirm network connectivity
  • Review replication configuration

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
mysql -e 'SHOW SLAVE STATUS\G'
psql -c 'SELECT * FROM pg_stat_replication;'

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm replication active
  2. Confirm replication lag within limits
  3. Verify data consistency

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Commvault provides enterprise backup, recovery, replication, archive, and data protection management.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review failed jobs
  • Check storage policy capacity
  • Confirm client connectivity
  • Validate deduplication database health
  • Review restore readiness

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
qoperation execute -af jobsummary.xml
qlist client
qlist storagepolicy
qoperation execscript -sn QS_CheckReadiness

docs.title: Upgrade Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm CommServe backup
  2. Verify client and media agent compatibility
  3. Upgrade CommServe
  4. Upgrade media agents
  5. Validate backup and restore operations

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: RecoverPoint provides continuous data protection and replication for block storage environments, enabling point-in-time recovery and disaster recovery operations.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify replication status
  • Check journal health
  • Confirm consistency group state
  • Review system alerts

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
get_system_status
get_group_status
get_cluster_status

docs.title: Failover Procedure
docs.text:
1. Identify recovery point
  2. Pause replication
  3. Enable image access
  4. Mount volumes to recovery hosts
  5. Validate application functionality

docs.title: Failback Procedure
docs.text:
1. Restore production environment
  2. Resume replication
  3. Synchronize journals
  4. Validate system health

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: SRDF (Symmetrix Remote Data Facility) provides synchronous and asynchronous replication between Dell PowerMax or VMAX storage arrays for disaster recovery.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify replication link status
  • Check pair state
  • Confirm synchronization health
  • Review alerts and logs

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
symrdf list
symrdf query
symcfg list
symdev show

docs.title: Failover Procedure
docs.text:
1. Confirm replication state is synchronized
  2. Suspend replication if required
  3. Promote target devices to read/write
  4. Mount storage to recovery hosts
  5. Validate application services

docs.title: Failback Procedure
docs.text:
1. Re-establish replication session
  2. Resynchronize data
  3. Validate storage state
  4. Restore normal production access

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure documents the process of returning workloads to the primary site after recovery operations.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Confirm primary site readiness
  2. Synchronize replication data
  3. Initiate failback
  4. Validate system stability
  5. Resume normal operations

docs.title: Post-Failback Checks
docs.text:
• Application functionality
  • Data integrity
  • Monitoring systems
  • Backup schedules

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure documents the controlled process of moving production workloads to a recovery site during an outage.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Confirm incident severity
  2. Validate replication status
  3. Initiate failover
  4. Verify system availability
  5. Notify stakeholders

docs.title: Post-Failover Checks
docs.text:
• Application health
  • Network connectivity
  • Monitoring alerts
  • Backup validation

docs.text: NetBackup provides enterprise backup and recovery for servers, databases, virtual machines, and large-scale production environments.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review failed jobs
  • Check storage unit capacity
  • Confirm catalog backup status
  • Validate media server health
  • Review policy schedules

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
bpdbjobs
bppllist
bpstulist
nbemmcmd -listhosts
bperror -backstat -hoursago 24

docs.title: Upgrade Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm master and media server compatibility
  2. Back up catalog
  3. Upgrade master server first
  4. Upgrade media servers and clients
  5. Validate backup and restore jobs

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook defines the standard steps to recover infrastructure and applications following a disaster or major outage.

docs.title: Activation Criteria
docs.text:
• Data center outage
  • Storage failure
  • Site-level network outage
  • Cybersecurity incident

docs.title: Recovery Steps
docs.text:
1. Declare disaster
  2. Notify stakeholders
  3. Initiate failover procedures
  4. Validate system recovery
  5. Restore business services

docs.title: Validation Checklist
docs.text:
• Systems operational
  • Data integrity confirmed
  • Monitoring restored
  • Users able to access services

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Veeam provides backup, replication, recovery, and disaster recovery capabilities for virtual, physical, and cloud workloads.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review failed backup jobs
  • Check repository capacity
  • Confirm restore points exist
  • Validate replication jobs
  • Review backup copy jobs

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
Get-VBRJob
Get-VBRBackup
Get-VBRRepository
Get-VBRSession | Sort-Object CreationTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 10

docs.title: Upgrade Workflow
docs.text:
1. Back up Veeam configuration database
  2. Confirm version compatibility
  3. Upgrade Veeam server
  4. Upgrade proxies and repositories if required
  5. Run test backup and restore validation

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: VMware Site Recovery Manager automates disaster recovery for VMware virtual machines using replication technologies and predefined recovery plans.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify SRM service status
  • Check protection group health
  • Validate recovery plans
  • Review replication status

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
service-control --status vmware-dr
dr-config status
dr-recovery-plan list

docs.title: Failover Procedure
docs.text:
1. Initiate recovery plan
  2. Monitor VM startup sequence
  3. Validate network connectivity
  4. Confirm application availability

docs.title: Failback Procedure
docs.text:
1. Reprotect workloads
  2. Synchronize replication
  3. Execute failback recovery plan
  4. Validate production services

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This checklist validates that infrastructure is ready to host new applications or workloads.

docs.title: Readiness Checks
docs.text:
• Capacity available
  • Network connectivity confirmed
  • Storage provisioned
  • Monitoring configured
  • Backup configured
  • Security policies applied

docs.title: Validation Commands
docs.text:
df -h
ping application-server
netstat -rn

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
• Infrastructure validated
  • Monitoring operational
  • Backup verified

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure defines steps to migrate systems or workloads between platforms, sites, or environments.

docs.title: Migration Steps
docs.text:
1. Confirm source system health
  2. Prepare destination environment
  3. Perform data synchronization
  4. Execute cutover
  5. Validate services

docs.title: Validation Commands
docs.text:
rsync -av source destination
ping destination-host
systemctl status

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
• Data synchronized
  • Services running
  • Users confirmed functionality

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure validates system health after an upgrade or patching activity.

docs.title: Validation Checklist
docs.text:
• Services running
  • Application connectivity verified
  • Monitoring alerts cleared
  • Performance metrics normal

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
systemctl status
netstat -tulnp
journalctl -p err -n 50

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
• Systems stable
  • No critical errors
  • Users confirmed functionality

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure restores systems to a previous stable state when changes fail.

docs.title: Rollback Steps
docs.text:
1. Identify failure point
  2. Restore backup or snapshot
  3. Restart services
  4. Validate system stability
  5. Notify stakeholders

docs.title: Validation Commands
docs.text:
restore backup-file
systemctl restart service

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
• System restored
  • Services stable
  • Incident documented

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure defines steps to safely remove systems from production environments.

docs.title: Required Steps
docs.text:
• Confirm system ownership approval
  • Verify data retention requirements
  • Remove system from monitoring
  • Remove backups
  • Shut down services
  • Update inventory records

docs.title: Validation Commands
docs.text:
shutdown now
systemctl disable service

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
• System powered off
  • Records updated
  • Access removed

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure defines steps to bring a new system into production management.

docs.title: Required Steps
docs.text:
• Assign hostname
  • Configure IP address
  • Join domain or directory
  • Install monitoring agent
  • Configure backup
  • Apply security baseline

docs.title: Validation Commands
docs.text:
hostname
ip addr
ping monitoring-server

docs.title: Completion Criteria
docs.text:
• System visible in monitoring
  • Backup job successful
  • Security policies applied

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This checklist validates that infrastructure is ready for a safe upgrade before changes begin.

docs.title: Pre-Upgrade Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm maintenance window approval
  • Verify backups completed successfully
  • Confirm rollback plan documented
  • Validate monitoring coverage
  • Confirm vendor compatibility matrix

docs.title: Validation Commands
docs.text:
df -h
uptime
ping gateway
systemctl --failed

docs.title: Go / No-Go Criteria
docs.text:
• All health checks passing
  • Backup verified
  • Support contacts available
  • Change approved

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Log retention policies define how long logs are stored to support compliance, auditing, and incident investigations.

docs.title: Standard Retention Periods
docs.text:
• System logs: 30–90 days
  • Security logs: 90–365 days
  • Audit logs: 1–7 years

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify log rotation working
  • Check storage capacity
  • Confirm archive jobs completed

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
logrotate -d /etc/logrotate.conf
df -h
ls -lh /var/log

docs.title: Validation Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm retention policy applied
  2. Validate rotation schedule
  3. Check archived logs accessible
  4. Verify compliance requirements met

docs.title: Daily Checks

  • Validate monitoring thresholds

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Centralized logging collects system and application logs for troubleshooting, auditing, and security monitoring.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify log ingestion
  • Check disk utilization on log servers
  • Confirm time synchronization

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
systemctl status rsyslog
df -h
tail -n 50 /var/log/messages
logger test-message

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm log service running
  2. Verify network connectivity to log collector
  3. Check log file permissions
  4. Validate time synchronization
  5. Review error logs

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook provides a structured process for diagnosing DNS resolution failures.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm hostname being queried
  • Confirm DNS server configuration
  • Verify network connectivity
  • Identify recent DNS changes

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
nslookup hostname
dig hostname
cat /etc/resolv.conf
ping dns-server

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm hostname resolves correctly
  2. Confirm application connectivity restored
  3. Monitor logs for repeated failures

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook verifies firewall rules allow required traffic.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm source and destination
  • Confirm port and protocol
  • Identify firewall device

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
nc -zv destination-host port
telnet destination-host port
ss -tulnp

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm connection allowed
  2. Confirm application connectivity restored
  3. Document firewall change if required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Firewalls control traffic between networks using rules, policies, zones, objects, and inspection profiles.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review blocked traffic logs
  • Validate rule hit counts
  • Check VPN tunnel health
  • Confirm policy changes
  • Review expired objects

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
show session all
show running security-policy
show log traffic
show system info

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm source, destination, port, and protocol
  2. Check policy match
  3. Review NAT rules
  4. Validate route path
  5. Review deny logs

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook validates load balancer health and backend availability.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm load balancer IP or hostname
  • Identify backend servers
  • Confirm service port

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
curl -I http://load-balancer
curl http://backend-server
netstat -tulnp

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm backend servers responding
  2. Confirm load balancer distributing traffic
  3. Monitor application response time

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Load balancers distribute traffic across multiple backend systems. They improve availability, scalability, and maintenance flexibility.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review pool member health
  • Check virtual server status
  • Validate certificates
  • Confirm persistence settings
  • Review error rates

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
curl -vk https://vip.example.com
openssl s_client -connect vip.example.com:443
dig vip.example.com

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm VIP is reachable
  2. Check pool member health
  3. Validate backend service ports
  4. Review SSL certificate state
  5. Check firewall path

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook identifies and resolves network connectivity issues between systems.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm source and destination systems
  • Verify IP addresses
  • Confirm routing configuration
  • Check firewall policies

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
ping destination-host
traceroute destination-host
ip route
netstat -rn

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm connectivity restored
  2. Confirm application communication functioning
  3. Document root cause

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook diagnoses packet loss affecting application performance.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm affected application
  • Identify network path
  • Check recent network changes

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
ping -c 100 destination-host
mtr destination-host
ethtool interface

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm packet loss resolved
  2. Confirm latency stabilized
  3. Monitor network performance metrics

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Routing determines how traffic moves between networks. It is required for server access, storage replication, cloud connectivity, backup traffic, and application communication.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm default gateway reachability
  • Review route tables
  • Check dynamic routing neighbor state
  • Validate critical path connectivity

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
ip route
route print
show ip route
show ip ospf neighbor
show bgp summary

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm source subnet
  2. Confirm destination subnet
  3. Check local route table
  4. Trace path
  5. Review firewall and ACL rules

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook verifies routing paths between network segments.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm destination network
  • Verify routing configuration
  • Identify gateway address

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
ip route show
traceroute destination-network
netstat -rn

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm correct routing path
  2. Confirm network reachability
  3. Document routing changes

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Subnetting divides IP networks into smaller address ranges. It is used for routing, segmentation, security boundaries, and capacity planning.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm available IP capacity
  • Validate subnet masks
  • Review overlapping networks
  • Confirm reserved addresses

docs.title: Useful Commands
docs.text:
ipcalc 10.10.10.0/24
ip addr
ip route
nslookup hostname

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm IP address
  2. Confirm subnet mask or CIDR
  3. Confirm default gateway
  4. Check for overlapping routes
  5. Validate reachability

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: TCP/IP is the core communication model used by servers, storage, cloud services, applications, and infrastructure platforms.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Verify host IP configuration
  • Confirm gateway reachability
  • Check DNS resolution
  • Validate service port connectivity

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
ip addr
ip route
ping 8.8.8.8
traceroute 8.8.8.8
nc -vz server 443

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm source and destination IPs
  2. Verify subnet and gateway
  3. Test DNS resolution
  4. Test port connectivity
  5. Check firewall rules

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: VLANs segment network traffic into logical broadcast domains. They are commonly used to separate management, storage, server, user, backup, and replication networks.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm VLAN exists on required switches
  • Verify trunk allowed VLANs
  • Check access port assignments
  • Validate tagging configuration

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
show vlan brief
show interfaces trunk
show interface status
show running-config interface INTERFACE

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm VLAN ID
  2. Check port mode access or trunk
  3. Verify VLAN allowed on trunk
  4. Confirm endpoint IP configuration
  5. Test connectivity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This procedure defines how to configure VLANs on network infrastructure.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm VLAN ID
  • Confirm network segment requirements
  • Verify switch configuration access

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
show vlan
show interface trunk
configure terminal

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm VLAN created
  2. Confirm devices assigned to VLAN
  3. Validate connectivity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: VPNs provide encrypted connectivity between users, sites, cloud environments, and partner networks.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm tunnel status
  • Review authentication failures
  • Check encryption settings
  • Validate route advertisements
  • Review certificate expiration

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
show vpn-sessiondb
show crypto ikev2 sa
show crypto ipsec sa
ping remote-subnet-ip

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm peer IP reachability
  2. Validate Phase 1 settings
  3. Validate Phase 2 settings
  4. Check routes and ACLs
  5. Review tunnel logs

  • Check CPU and memory trends
  • Validate backup repository growth
  • Review cloud spend trends

  • Forecasted exhaustion date
  • Reserved capacity
  • Peak utilization

  3. Identify exhaustion dates
  4. Document risks
  5. Plan expansion or cleanup

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Health checks provide repeatable validation of infrastructure platforms before, during, and after operational changes.

docs.title: Standard Checklist
docs.text:
• Alerts reviewed
  • Capacity reviewed
  • Performance reviewed
  • Replication reviewed
  • Backup reviewed
  • Logs reviewed
  • Certificates reviewed

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Run platform-specific checks
  2. Document findings
  3. Assign remediation items
  4. Re-check after fixes
  5. Save results for audit history

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Incident response is the process of detecting, triaging, resolving, and documenting service-impacting events.

docs.title: Triage Checklist
docs.text:
• Confirm affected service
  • Identify business impact
  • Check recent changes
  • Review monitoring alerts
  • Assign owner

docs.title: Response Workflow
docs.text:
1. Detect issue
  2. Confirm impact
  3. Stabilize service
  4. Identify root cause
  5. Document RCA and follow-up actions

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Maintenance windows provide controlled time periods for planned infrastructure changes, upgrades, patching, and validation.

docs.title: Planning Checklist
docs.text:
• Confirm business approval
  • Validate backup and rollback plan
  • Identify impacted systems
  • Notify stakeholders
  • Confirm support contacts

docs.title: Execution Workflow
docs.text:
1. Start change bridge
  2. Confirm pre-checks
  3. Execute change
  4. Validate systems
  5. Communicate completion

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Patch management keeps operating systems, applications, firmware, and infrastructure platforms secure and stable.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Review missing critical patches
  • Confirm failed patch jobs
  • Check reboot pending status
  • Review maintenance windows

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
Get-HotFix
Get-CimInstance Win32_QuickFixEngineering

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Review patch scope
  2. Confirm backups
  3. Patch non-production first
  4. Patch production during approved window
  5. Validate services after reboot

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: NTP keeps infrastructure time synchronized. Time drift can break authentication, certificates, logging, replication, clustering, and audit trails.

docs.title: Daily Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm time source is reachable
  • Check drift offset
  • Validate domain time hierarchy
  • Review time sync errors

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
ntpq -p
chronyc sources
timedatectl status
w32tm /query /status

docs.title: Upgrade Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm authoritative time sources
  2. Update NTP or chrony configuration
  3. Restart time service
  4. Validate offset and synchronization
  5. Monitor logs for drift warnings

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook covers renewing and validating certificates used by applications and infrastructure services.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm certificate expiration date
  • Identify certificate owner
  • Confirm issuing CA
  • Confirm services using the certificate

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text -noout
openssl s_client -connect server:443
curl -vk https://server

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Install renewed certificate
  2. Restart affected service
  3. Validate TLS connection
  4. Confirm monitoring alert cleared

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook helps identify and clean up disk space issues safely.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm affected filesystem
  • Identify largest directories
  • Avoid deleting application data without approval

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
df -h
du -sh /* 2>/dev/null | sort -h
find /var/log -type f -name '*.gz' -mtime +30
journalctl --disk-usage

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm free space improved
  2. Confirm application still running
  3. Document files removed

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook provides a safe process for rebooting servers during maintenance or troubleshooting.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm maintenance approval
  • Verify backups completed
  • Check logged-in users
  • Confirm application owner awareness

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
who
uptime
systemctl --failed
sudo reboot

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm server responds to ping
  2. Confirm SSH or RDP access
  3. Validate services
  4. Review system logs

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook provides a controlled process for restarting infrastructure or application services.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm service owner approval
  • Check active users or jobs
  • Review recent alerts
  • Confirm rollback plan

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
systemctl status service-name
systemctl restart service-name
systemctl status service-name
journalctl -u service-name -n 50

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm service running
  2. Check application response
  3. Review logs
  4. Confirm monitoring is clear

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook provides a controlled process for expanding storage volumes.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm requested size
  • Validate pool capacity
  • Confirm host multipathing
  • Confirm filesystem expansion plan

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
df -h
lsblk
multipath -ll

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Expand storage volume
  2. Rescan host storage
  3. Expand filesystem
  4. Confirm application sees new capacity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook defines safe use of VM snapshots before changes.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm VM owner approval
  • Check existing snapshots
  • Confirm datastore capacity
  • Define snapshot removal time

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
vim-cmd vmsvc/getallvms
vim-cmd vmsvc/snapshot.get VMID
vim-cmd vmsvc/snapshot.create VMID pre-change '' 0 0

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm snapshot created
  2. Complete change
  3. Remove snapshot after validation
  4. Confirm snapshot consolidation is clean

repadmin /replsummary

docs.text:
• Malware infection
  • Unauthorized access
  • Data breach
  • Suspicious network activity

docs.title: Response Workflow
docs.text:
1. Detect incident
  2. Contain threat
  3. Investigate cause
  4. Restore services
  5. Document incident

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Authentication failures may occur due to directory service issues, credential problems, certificate errors, or network connectivity problems.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Login failures
  • Account lockouts
  • Expired passwords
  • Kerberos errors

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
Get-EventLog -LogName Security -Newest 20
nltest /dsgetdc:domain
klist

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm user credentials
  2. Verify domain controller availability
  3. Check time synchronization
  4. Review security logs
  5. Reset credentials if required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Backup failures increase risk of data loss and recovery delays during outages.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Failed backup jobs
  • Missing restore points
  • Repository errors
  • Network timeouts

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
Get-VBRJob
bpdbjobs
qlist job

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify failed job
  2. Review error logs
  3. Validate storage capacity
  4. Confirm network connectivity
  5. Retry backup job

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: DNS failures prevent applications, servers, and services from locating required resources.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Unable to resolve hostname
  • Application connection errors
  • Service startup failures

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
nslookup hostname
dig hostname
ipconfig /flushdns

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm DNS server configuration
  2. Validate network connectivity
  3. Check DNS records
  4. Restart DNS service if required
  5. Test resolution again

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: High CPU utilization can cause performance degradation, latency, and service instability across applications and infrastructure.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• System slow response
  • High load average
  • Application timeouts
  • Monitoring alerts

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
top
htop
ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head
uptime

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify process consuming CPU
  2. Confirm recent changes or deployments
  3. Review logs
  4. Validate resource limits
  5. Restart or scale service if required

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Network connectivity failures prevent systems from communicating across services, storage, and cloud environments.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Unable to reach server
  • Packet loss
  • Application connection failure
  • Timeout errors

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
ping host
traceroute host
ip addr
ip route

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm IP configuration
  2. Validate gateway connectivity
  3. Check routing tables
  4. Review firewall rules
  5. Validate DNS resolution

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Replication failures can impact disaster recovery readiness and data consistency.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Replication lag
  • Synchronization errors
  • Failover readiness warnings

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
snapmirror show
symrdf query
get_group_status

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Verify replication link status
  2. Check network connectivity
  3. Review storage capacity
  4. Confirm configuration settings
  5. Resume replication

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Storage latency impacts application response times, database performance, and VM operations.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Slow disk operations
  • VM performance degradation
  • Database timeouts
  • Increased I/O wait

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
iostat -x 5
vmstat 5
esxtop
symstat

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Confirm latency metrics
  2. Identify impacted volumes or LUNs
  3. Check host connectivity
  4. Review storage alerts
  5. Validate replication or snapshot activity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Virtual machine performance issues may be caused by CPU contention, memory pressure, storage latency, or network congestion.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Slow application response
  • High CPU ready time
  • Memory swapping
  • Disk latency alerts

docs.title: Health Commands
docs.text:
esxtop
vmstat
top
free -m

docs.title: Troubleshooting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Check CPU and memory utilization
  2. Review storage latency
  3. Confirm network connectivity
  4. Review recent changes
  5. Adjust resource allocation if needed

docs.title: Virtualization
docs.text:
Virtualization support notes for VMware, VxRail, Aria, health checks, troubleshooting, standards, inventory, runbooks, and upgrade readiness.

VMware Platform vCenter, ESXi, vSAN, NSX, VCF, Aria Suite, lifecycle, troubleshooting, and operations. VxRail VxRail Manager, lifecycle, hardware, support bundles, upgrades, and validation. Operations Health checks, troubleshooting guides, and runbooks for the virtualization platform. Reference Standards, inventory, upgrade readiness checklists, and quick reference material.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Operational procedures, health checks, troubleshooting guides, and runbooks for the virtualization platform.

Health Checks

Pre- and post-change health checks, daily checks, and validation procedures.

Troubleshooting

Troubleshooting guides, known issues, and resolution steps across all platforms.

Runbooks

Step-by-step operational runbooks for common tasks and incidents.

docs.title: Virtualization Health Checks
docs.text:
Reusable health checks for virtualization operations.

Daily Health Check Daily checks across vCenter, ESXi, vSAN, NSX, VxRail, and Aria. Pre-Change Check Checks before maintenance, patching, upgrades, migrations, or config changes. Post-Change Validation Validation after maintenance, upgrades, patching, or configuration changes. Capacity Review Cluster, datastore, vSAN, CPU, memory, and growth review. Alert Review Review active alerts, stale alerts, ownership, and escalation needs. Management Access Check vCenter, ESXi, VxRail Manager, NSX, and Aria access validation.

docs.title: Active Alerts Review
docs.text:
• Review all critical alerts in vCenter — confirm each has an owner or action
  • Review warning alerts — identify any that have been open longer than expected
  • Check for alerts that triggered during a recent maintenance window

docs.title: Aria Operations Alerts
docs.text:
• Review Aria Operations alert dashboard
  • Identify any critical or high-severity alerts
  • Confirm alerts are not suppressed unnecessarily outside maintenance windows

docs.title: Hardware Alerts
docs.text:
• Review iDRAC alerts for all VxRail nodes and other servers
  • Confirm no outstanding disk, memory, NIC, or PSU alerts

docs.title: Backup Alerts
docs.text:
• Review backup platform for failed or missed jobs
  • Confirm all critical VMs and systems have a successful recent backup

docs.title: Repeat Alerts
docs.text:
• Identify alerts that fire repeatedly without resolution
  • Review repeat alerts for tuning or permanent fixes
  • Suppress intentionally only with a documented reason and expiry

docs.title: False Positives and Stale Alerts
docs.text:
• Remove or disable alerts that no longer apply
  • Review alert thresholds — adjust if consistently firing below the meaningful threshold

docs.title: Alert Owner and Next Action
docs.text: For each open critical alert, confirm: - Owner assigned - Next action documented - Escalation path clear if not resolved within SLA

docs.title: Capacity Checks
docs.text:
Capacity should be reviewed regularly to avoid outages and emergency cleanups.

  • Cluster CPU usage
  • Cluster memory usage
  • Datastore free space
  • vSAN usable capacity
  • Snapshot growth
  • Thin-provisioned risk
  • VM disk growth
  • Log volume growth
  • Backup repository usage

docs.title: Daily Health Check
docs.text:
Daily checks should focus on items that can impact availability quickly.

Area Check vCenter Confirm vCenter is reachable and services are healthy ESXi Hosts Confirm all hosts are connected Clusters Check HA, DRS, and admission control Datastores Confirm free space and latency vSAN Review Skyline Health, disk groups, resyncs, and object health VMs Check critical VM status, snapshots, and VMware Tools Alerts Review active critical and warning alarms Backups Confirm backup jobs completed Access Confirm admin login and identity source health

docs.title: Access Checks
docs.text:
• Review local administrator access
  • Review vCenter roles and permissions
  • Confirm AD/LDAP identity source health
  • Remove stale accounts
  • Validate service accounts
  • Confirm MFA or privileged access controls if used
  • Monitor failed logins
  • Protect break-glass accounts

docs.title: Post-Change Checks
docs.text:
Post-change checks confirm the environment is healthy after work is complete.

  • Confirm all hosts are connected
  • Confirm cluster HA and DRS status
  • Confirm VMs are running as expected
  • Confirm datastores are accessible
  • Confirm vSAN health is green
  • Confirm no unexpected new alerts
  • Confirm backup jobs still run
  • Confirm monitoring is receiving data
  • Confirm application owner validation if needed
  • Update change record with evidence

docs.title: Pre-Change Checks
docs.text:
Pre-change checks confirm the platform is healthy before maintenance begins.

  • Confirm vCenter access
  • Confirm ESXi host connectivity
  • Check active alarms
  • Confirm no unexpected host maintenance mode
  • Check datastore free space
  • Confirm no stuck snapshots
  • Confirm backup status
  • Check vSAN health if applicable
  • Confirm NTP and DNS health
  • Confirm rollback plan
  • Capture current versions
  • Confirm maintenance window approval

docs.title: Virtualization Runbooks
docs.text:
Practical runbooks for incidents, maintenance, lifecycle work, validation, evidence collection, and RCA follow-up.

Incident Response Use this during virtualization incidents where VMs, hosts, clusters, datastores, networking, or management tools are impacted. Maintenance Window Runbook Use this for planned work across VMware, VxRail, NSX, Aria, hosts, clusters, or related services. Host Evacuation Runbook Use this before host maintenance, patching, hardware work, or lifecycle activity. VM Snapshot Cleanup Runbook Use this to find and clean up old or risky VM snapshots. VM Lifecycle Runbook Use this for VM build, change, ownership, review, retirement, and cleanup. Storage Path Validation Use this after SAN changes, storage maintenance, host work, or datastore alerts. Network Validation Use this after network changes, VLAN changes, host work, NSX changes, or VM connectivity issues. Certificate Renewal Planning Use this before vCenter, NSX, VxRail, Aria, or related certificate renewals. Evidence Collection Use this before vendor escalation, RCA work, or major incident review. RCA Template Use this after a virtualization incident or recurring problem.

docs.title: Identify Failed VMs
docs.text:
• Review the backup platform for failed or missed backup jobs
  • Note the VM name, backup job name, error message, and failure time

docs.title: Review the Error Message
docs.text: Common backup errors: - Snapshot creation failure - Snapshot consolidation warning - Datastore out of space - Network or proxy connectivity failure - vCenter API error

docs.title: Check VM Snapshot State
docs.text:
• In vCenter: right-click the VM → Snapshots → Manage Snapshots
  • Confirm no stale backup snapshots are present
  • If consolidation is needed: right-click VM → Snapshots → Consolidate

docs.title: Check Datastore Free Space
docs.text:
• Confirm the datastore hosting the VM has sufficient free space
  • Free space less than 10% can block snapshot creation

docs.title: Check Backup Proxy Health
docs.text:
• Confirm the backup proxy VM is powered on and reachable
  • Review proxy logs in the backup platform

docs.title: Check Backup Repository
docs.text:
• Confirm the backup repository has sufficient free space
  • Confirm the repository is accessible from the proxy

docs.title: Check vCenter Permissions
docs.text:
• Confirm the backup service account has the required vCenter permissions
  • Review vCenter roles and recent permission changes

docs.title: Retry the Backup
docs.text:
• If the root cause is resolved, manually retry the backup job
  • Monitor the retry and confirm it completes successfully

docs.title: Escalate Recurring Failures
docs.text:
• If the same VM fails repeatedly, escalate to the backup platform team
  • Open a support case with the backup vendor if needed

docs.title: Document Resolution
docs.text:
• Update the backup platform job notes with the root cause and fix
  • Update the incident ticket with findings and resolution

docs.title: Identify the Expiring Certificate
docs.text:
• Review certificate inventory
  • Confirm the certificate type: Machine SSL, STS, solution user, or integration endpoint
  • Note the affected product and expiration date

docs.title: Confirm Affected Products
docs.text:
• List all products that trust or use this certificate
  • Confirm which integrations may be disrupted during replacement

docs.title: Capture Current Certificate Details
docs.text:
• Subject, SAN, issuer, expiration date
  • Screenshot from VAMI or vSphere Client as pre-change evidence

docs.title: Confirm Backup Exists
docs.text:
• Confirm vCenter file-based backup is current
  • Confirm product backup for Aria or NSX if their certificate is being replaced

docs.title: Schedule Maintenance Window
docs.text:
• Plan replacement outside peak hours
  • Allow time for service restarts and integration validation

docs.title: Replace the Certificate
docs.text:
• Follow the correct replacement method for the certificate type
  • For VMCA-issued certs: use vSphere Client or VAMI
  • For custom CA certs: generate CSR, submit to CA, import signed cert

docs.title: Restart Required Services
docs.text:
service-control --restart --all

Only restart services after confirming the new certificate is applied.

docs.title: Validate Integrations
docs.text:
• vCenter browser access — no certificate warning
  • SSO login for local and AD accounts
  • Aria, NSX, backup, and monitoring integrations confirmed

docs.title: Document Final Expiration Date
docs.text:
• Update the certificate inventory with the new expiration date
  • Set a review reminder 60 days before the new expiration

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use this before vendor escalation, RCA work, or major incident review.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm issue scope.
  • Confirm affected objects.
  • Confirm timestamps.
  • Confirm recent changes.
  • Confirm ticket or case number if available.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Capture screenshots of alarms.
  2. Export recent tasks and events.
  3. Capture affected object names.
  4. Capture timestamps and timezone.
  5. Collect support bundles if needed.
  6. Record commands already run.
  7. Record impact and current status.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Evidence is complete enough for handoff.
  • Timeline is clear.
  • Affected systems are listed.
  • Next owner has what they need.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Stop the change if impact increases.
  • Return settings to the last known good state where possible.
  • Reconnect affected systems if disconnected.
  • Escalate with logs, timestamps, screenshots, and task IDs.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Keep this page updated with local commands, screenshots, system names, and known environment quirks.

docs.title: Confirm Impact
docs.text:
• Identify the affected host
  • Check vCenter — is the host Disconnected, Not Responding, or in Error?
  • Identify which VMs were running on the host
  • Confirm HA status — have VMs been restarted on other hosts?

docs.title: Check Power State
docs.text:
• Log into iDRAC and confirm power state
  • If powered off unexpectedly, check power supply health and power events in iDRAC

docs.title: Check Management Network
docs.text:
• Ping the host management IP
  • Check DNS forward and reverse lookup for the hostname
  • Confirm the management switch port is active

docs.title: Check Hardware Management Interface
docs.text:
• Log into iDRAC and review hardware health
  • Check for disk, memory, NIC, or PSU failures
  • Review Lifecycle Controller logs for recent hardware events

docs.title: Review vCenter Alarms
docs.text:
• Confirm which alarms are active on the host
  • Check related cluster and datastore alarms

docs.title: Identify Affected VMs
docs.text:
• Confirm which VMs were running on the failed host
  • Verify HA has restarted critical VMs on other hosts
  • Check application owners for any workloads that did not restart

docs.title: Logs to Collect
docs.text:
• iDRAC hardware logs and screenshots
  • vCenter events from the time of the failure
  • ESXi host logs if accessible via SSH or support bundle
  • Aria Operations alerts at the time of failure

docs.title: Engage Hardware Support
docs.text:
• Open a Dell support case if hardware failure is confirmed
  • Provide iDRAC logs, hardware event screenshots, and host serial number

docs.title: Validate Cluster Health After Recovery
docs.text:
• Confirm all remaining hosts are Connected
  • Confirm HA and DRS are active
  • Confirm vSAN object health is green if vSAN is used
  • Confirm VMs are running on healthy hosts
  • Update the change or incident ticket with findings

docs.title: Incident Response Runbook
docs.text: Use this when there is an active VMware platform issue.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Confirm the issue scope
  2. Identify impacted systems
  3. Check vCenter availability
  4. Check host and cluster health
  5. Review active alarms
  6. Check recent tasks and events
  7. Check datastore and vSAN health
  8. Check network health
  9. Check hardware alerts
  10. Review logs
  11. Escalate if needed
  12. Document findings
  13. Confirm recovery
  14. Communicate status
  15. Complete RCA if required

docs.title: Evidence to Capture
docs.text:
• Date and time of issue
  • Impacted VMs, hosts, clusters, or datastores
  • Screenshots of alarms
  • Recent vCenter events
  • Logs from vCenter or ESXi
  • Support bundles if needed
  • Timeline of actions taken
  • Validation after recovery

docs.title: Maintenance Window Runbook
docs.text: Use this for planned VMware work.

docs.title: Before Maintenance
docs.text:
• Review change ticket
  • Confirm maintenance window
  • Notify stakeholders
  • Confirm backups
  • Confirm current health
  • Confirm rollback plan
  • Capture versions
  • Confirm access
  • Confirm vendor support if needed

docs.title: During Maintenance
docs.text:
• Start maintenance window
  • Place host in maintenance mode if required
  • Perform approved work
  • Monitor cluster and workload health
  • Capture screenshots or logs
  • Escalate if unexpected issues occur

docs.title: After Maintenance
docs.text:
• Validate cluster health
  • Confirm VMs are running
  • Confirm datastores are accessible
  • Confirm monitoring is clean
  • Confirm backups still work
  • Update ticket with results
  • Send completion notice

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use this after network changes, VLAN changes, host work, NSX changes, or VM connectivity issues.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm affected VLANs or segments.
  • Confirm port groups or NSX segments.
  • Confirm uplink status.
  • Confirm recent switch or firewall changes.
  • Confirm affected VM scope.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Check VM network assignment.
  2. Check port group or segment configuration.
  3. Check host uplinks.
  4. Check VLAN or overlay configuration.
  5. Check gateway reachability.
  6. Check NSX edge and routing if used.
  7. Test from affected and unaffected VMs.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• VM connectivity works.
  • Uplinks are healthy.
  • VLAN or segment config is correct.
  • Routing is working.
  • No new network alarms.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Stop the change if impact increases.
  • Return settings to the last known good state where possible.
  • Reconnect affected systems if disconnected.
  • Escalate with logs, timestamps, screenshots, and task IDs.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Keep this page updated with local commands, screenshots, system names, and known environment quirks.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Brief description of what happened.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text: Systems, users, applications, or services affected.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: Time Event HH:MM Issue detected HH:MM Investigation started HH:MM Cause identified HH:MM Fix applied HH:MM Service restored

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text: Explain the actual cause of the issue.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: Explain what was done to fix it.

docs.title: Prevention
docs.text: List steps to reduce the chance of the issue happening again.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Attach logs, screenshots, events, support case numbers, and validation results.

docs.title: Confirm vSAN Health State
docs.text:
• Open vCenter → Cluster → vSAN → Skyline Health
  • Identify which health checks are failing
  • Open Virtual Objects view and filter by Degraded, Non-compliant, or Absent

docs.title: Identify Affected Objects
docs.text:
• Note the VM name, object type, and storage policy for each affected object
  • Check if the VM is still running or if it has failed

docs.title: Check Failed Disks
docs.text:
• Review Skyline Health → Physical Disk section
  • Check iDRAC for disk health on all VxRail nodes

docs.title: Check Host Availability
docs.text:
• Confirm all hosts are Connected in vCenter
  • Check if any host is in maintenance mode unexpectedly

docs.title: Check Resync Status
docs.text:
esxcli vsan debug resync summary get

Active resync is expected after a host returns from maintenance — wait for it to complete before taking further action.

docs.title: Check Capacity
docs.text:
• Confirm vSAN usable capacity is within safe limits
  • If capacity is the cause of non-compliance, expansion may be needed

docs.title: Review Storage Policy
docs.text:
• Confirm the storage policy assigned to affected objects is achievable with current cluster state
  • If FTT=1 and only one host or disk is available, the policy cannot be met

docs.title: Avoid Unsafe Actions
docs.text:
• Do not take additional hosts into maintenance mode while objects are degraded
  • Do not delete VMs or disks without VMware support guidance

docs.title: Engage VMware Support
docs.text:
• Collect a vSAN support bundle if objects remain degraded after the expected recovery period
  • Open a VMware support case and provide the bundle, timeline, and Skyline Health screenshots

docs.title: Validate Object Compliance After Recovery
docs.text:
• Return to Virtual Objects view and confirm all objects are Healthy
  • Run Skyline Health and confirm no remaining failures

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use this after SAN changes, storage maintenance, host work, or datastore alerts.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm affected hosts and datastores.
  • Confirm storage array status.
  • Confirm SAN zoning or masking changes.
  • Confirm no active datastore outage.
  • Confirm maintenance window if changes are planned.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Check datastore visibility.
  2. Check host storage adapters.
  3. Check path count and path state.
  4. Check multipathing policy.
  5. Review storage latency.
  6. Confirm VMs can access datastores.
  7. Compare against expected path design.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Expected paths are visible.
  • No dead paths remain unless expected.
  • Datastores are mounted.
  • Latency is normal.
  • No new storage alarms.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Stop the change if impact increases.
  • Return settings to the last known good state where possible.
  • Reconnect affected systems if disconnected.
  • Escalate with logs, timestamps, screenshots, and task IDs.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Keep this page updated with local commands, screenshots, system names, and known environment quirks.

docs.title: Confirm Outage Scope
docs.text:
• Can you access the vSphere Client?
  • Can you ping the vCenter FQDN and IP?
  • Are ESXi hosts still visible and running workloads independently?

docs.title: Check VCSA VM Power State
docs.text:
• Confirm the VCSA VM is powered on in vCenter (if a secondary vCenter is available)
  • Or verify via iDRAC/IPMI if the VCSA is running on a known host

docs.title: Check VCSA Appliance Management
docs.text:
• Access https://<vcenter>:5480
  • Review service health, disk partitions, and CPU/memory

docs.title: Check DNS and Network Reachability
docs.text:
ping <vcenter-ip>
nslookup <vcenter-fqdn>

docs.title: Check Service Status
docs.text:
# SSH to vCenter appliance
service-control --status

docs.title: Check Disk Partitions
docs.text:
df -h

Partitions that commonly cause failures when full: - /storage/log - /storage/db

docs.title: Review Recent Changes
docs.text:
• Was a certificate recently replaced?
  • Was a patch or upgrade recently applied?
  • Was a snapshot taken or deleted on the VCSA VM?

docs.title: Restore from Backup if Required
docs.text:
• Use the vCenter file-based backup (VAMI → Backup)
  • Confirm the backup date and restore target
  • Follow VMware restore documentation

docs.title: Validate Services After Recovery
docs.text:
• Confirm all services are running: service-control --status
  • Confirm vSphere Client is accessible
  • Confirm all hosts are reconnecting
  • Confirm Aria and other integrations are working

docs.title: Communicate Impact
docs.text:
• Notify stakeholders of the outage and recovery status
  • Note that ESXi hosts and VMs continue running without vCenter
  • Update the incident ticket with timeline and resolution

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use this for VM build, change, ownership, review, retirement, and cleanup.

docs.title: Pre-Checks
docs.text:
• Confirm VM owner.
  • Confirm business purpose.
  • Confirm sizing.
  • Confirm backup policy.
  • Confirm monitoring.
  • Confirm network and security requirements.
  • Confirm naming standard.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Validate request details.
  2. Build or update VM.
  3. Apply naming and tagging standards.
  4. Confirm backup and monitoring.
  5. Validate access and connectivity.
  6. Record owner and lifecycle notes.
  7. Review unused VMs regularly.
  8. Decommission cleanly when approved.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• VM has owner.
  • VM follows naming standard.
  • Backup is assigned.
  • Monitoring is active.
  • Tags or inventory notes are current.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Stop the change if impact increases.
  • Return settings to the last known good state where possible.
  • Reconnect affected systems if disconnected.
  • Escalate with logs, timestamps, screenshots, and task IDs.

docs.title: Virtualization Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common virtualization troubleshooting workflows.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Flow
docs.text:
Start by defining the scope, then work down through the stack.

  1. Define scope — one VM, one host, one cluster, or full vCenter outage?
  2. Check vCenter health — can you log in? Are services running? Any critical alarms?
  3. Check host health — are all hosts connected? Any in warning or not responding?
  4. Check storage and vSAN — are datastores accessible? Is vSAN Skyline Health green?
  5. Check network — are VM and management networks reachable? Any vMotion failures?
  6. Review recent tasks and events — what changed in the last 24 hours?
  7. Check logs — hostd, vpxa, vmkernel, vCenter events, Aria for Logs
  8. Escalate — open a Dell or VMware support case if the root cause is unclear
VM Performance Issue First-pass workflow for CPU, memory, storage, and network symptoms. Host Disconnected Workflow for disconnected or not responding ESXi hosts. Datastore Inaccessible Troubleshooting VMFS, NFS, vSAN, and storage visibility issues. Network Connectivity Issue VM, host, VLAN, distributed switch, and NSX connectivity checks. Certificate Issue vCenter, NSX, VxRail, and Aria certificate symptoms and workflow. Login or Access Issue SSO, LDAP, AD, permissions, MFA, and local account checks.

docs.title: Common Certificate Issues
docs.text: Symptom What to Check Browser certificate warning vCenter machine certificate Login issues STS certificate, SSO service, identity source Product integration broken Trusted root chain, expired certs Aria connection failure Endpoint certificate trust NSX registration issue Certificate thumbprint or trust relationship

docs.text: Symptom What to Check Datastore full Snapshots, ISO files, orphaned VMDKs, old templates High latency Array performance, queue depth, paths, congestion Datastore inaccessible SAN zoning, LUN masking, paths, storage controller VMFS issue Locks, resignature, extent health vSAN object warning Storage policy, resync, disk group, capacity

docs.title: Common Host Issues
docs.text: Symptom What to Check Host disconnected Management IP, DNS, vmk0, hostd, vpxa Host not responding Network, PSOD, hardware, management services Host cannot enter maintenance mode Running VMs, DRS, pinned VMs, vSAN evacuation Host hardware warning iDRAC/iLO, PSU, disk, memory, NIC, firmware Host time drift NTP service, time source, firewall

docs.title: Common Login Issues
docs.text: Symptom What to Check Cannot log into vCenter SSO service, identity source, locked account AD users cannot log in LDAP/LDAPS, domain controller, DNS, time sync Local admin works but AD does not Identity source or AD connectivity Permission denied vCenter role assignment, group membership Session timeout Browser cache, SSO token, service health

docs.title: Common Network Issues
docs.text: Symptom What to Check vMotion fails VMkernel adapter, MTU, VLAN, routing, license VM network outage Port group, VLAN, physical uplink, NIC teaming Host management issue vmk0, gateway, DNS, management VLAN NSX issue TEP status, transport nodes, edges, segments Packet loss Physical switch, NIC, MTU, congestion

docs.title: Common VM Issues
docs.text: Symptom What to Check VM will not power on Host resources, datastore space, lock files, HA status VM is slow CPU ready, memory ballooning, datastore latency, snapshots VM lost network Port group, VLAN, VMXNET3 adapter, VMware Tools VM disk full Guest OS disk usage, snapshots, thin disk growth VMware Tools warning Tools version, guest OS support, pending reboot

docs.title: Host Disconnected
docs.text:
Cause:

  • Network issue
  • DNS issue
  • Host service failure

Fix:

  • Verify management network
  • Restart management agents
  • Validate DNS resolution

docs.title: vSAN Capacity Warning
docs.text:
Cause:

  • Low free capacity
  • Large resync operation

Fix:

  • Review capacity
  • Delay maintenance
  • Add capacity if required

docs.title: vCenter Login Failure
docs.text:
Cause:

  • SSO issue
  • Certificate issue

Fix:

  • Check SSO services
  • Validate certificates
  • Review authentication logs

docs.text:
1. Log into vCenter
  2. Check active alarms
  3. Confirm all hosts are connected
  4. Check cluster HA and DRS status

docs.title: First Decision
docs.text:
Can you ping host?

No → Check network

Yes → Check management services

If services stopped → Restart agents

If still down → Escalate hardware

docs.title: First Decision
docs.text:
Can VM ping gateway?

No → Check VLAN or segment

Yes → Check routing

If routing OK → Check firewall

If firewall OK → Check packet loss

docs.title: First Decision
docs.text:
Is latency > 20 ms?

Yes → Check resync

If resync active → Wait

If not → Check storage array

If array healthy → Check network

docs.title: First Decision
docs.text:
Is CPU high?

Yes → Check CPU Ready

No → Check Memory

Is Memory Ballooning?

Yes → Add memory or move workload

No → Check Storage Latency

If latency high → Investigate storage

Backups Are recent backups available?

docs.text:
Before escalation, collect:

  • Host name
  • VM name
